verses.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus our Lord? Aren’t you proof of my work for the Lord?
If other people don’t count me as an apostle, you at least do. You’re the seal on my apostleship in the Lord.
Here’s my answer to the people questioning me:
Don’t we have the right to food and drink?
Don’t we have the right to travel with a believing wife, like the other apostles, the Lord’s brothers, and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who have to keep working for a living?
What soldier pays all their own expenses? Who plants a vineyard and doesn’t eat its fruit? Who tends a flock and doesn’t drink its milk?
Am I just making this up from human custom? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
Moses’ Law says, “Don’t muzzle an ox while it’s threshing grain.” Is God only concerned about oxen?
Surely he’s talking about us too. The person plowing should plow with hope, and the one threshing should expect a share of the harvest.
If we planted spiritual things among you, is it too much to harvest material support from you?
If others can claim this support from you, don’t we have an even stronger claim? Still, we haven’t used that right. We put up with everything so we wouldn’t block the Good News about Christ.
Don’t you know temple workers eat from the temple’s offerings, and people serving at the altar share in what’s offered there?
In the same way, the Lord directed that people who preach the Good News should be supported by it.
But I haven’t used any of these rights. I’m not writing this to get support from you. I’d rather die than let anyone take this reason for boasting away from me.
If I preach the Good News, I can’t brag about that—it’s my assignment. How terrible for me if I don’t preach it!
If I chose this work myself, I’d have a reward coming. But whether I chose it or not, I’ve been entrusted with a responsibility.
So what’s my reward? I get to share the Good News free of charge and not use up my rights as a preacher.
Even though I’m free from everyone, I made myself everyone’s servant so I could reach more people.
With Jewish people, I lived like a Jew so I could reach Jewish people. With those under the Law, I lived as one under the Law—even though I’m not under it—so I could reach them.
With people outside the Law, I lived like someone outside it—not outside God’s law, but under Christ’s law—so I could reach them.
With people who are weak, I became weak so I could reach them. I’ve adapted to all kinds of people so that by every means some might be saved.
I do all this for the sake of the Good News, so I can share in its blessings.
Don’t you know that everybody in a race runs, but only one gets the prize? So run to win.
Every athlete in training exercises self-control. They do it for a crown that fades; we do it for one that lasts forever. 🏅
So I’m not running without a goal. I’m not shadowboxing the air.
I train my body and make it obey, so after preaching to others, I won’t end up disqualified myself.
